evidence: "# 1. bipartition" and the statement's warning that "solutions may contain gears from both camps"
affordance_in_statement: The gears can be perfectly divided into two camps, and every engagement point connects one gear from each camp; solutions may contain gears from both camps.
removal_suggestion: No task-preserving removal is available. The bipartite structure is the core mathematical property, and a correct solver can use maximum matching/minimum vertex cover to construct a maximum independent set, then truncate it to exactly k vertices.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Uses the bipartite structure to solve maximum independent set rather than assuming the answer is one color class; an independent set of size at least k can then be reduced to exactly k vertices.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The graph is guaranteed bipartite, while the statement explicitly allows valid selections to contain vertices from both camps.

common_affordance: The guaranteed bipartite graph structure enabling a matching-based maximum-independent-set solution

defeated_student_causes.why_failed: It bipartitions the graph but treats a color class, or the larger color class, as the relevant feasible set, ignoring independent sets formed from vertices in both camps.
Its approach is side-based after bipartitioning, so it can reject or construct incorrectly when the largest independent set is not a single camp.
It builds component bipartitions and relies on camp sizes rather than computing the exact maximum independent-set size and witness for the whole graph.

recommended_edit: Make no edit: no mutable wording change can defeat the surviving correct matching-based algorithm without changing the core problem. Rephrasing the two-camp guarantee would not remove the underlying bipartite structure.
